description: Area C is over 60% of the West Bank and is under full Israeli civil and security control. Palestinians may build in less than 1% of it.
energy_note: Sixty per cent of the land, one per cent of it available.

aspect: It is where the utilities have to go
description: Water mains, power lines, telecom masts, roads and sewage all have to cross Area C to connect anything to anything. Refusing permits there constrains development in Areas A and B without touching them.
energy_note: Control the middle and you control both ends.

description: Palestinian operators cannot readily erect towers in Area C, which is why coverage and capacity are poor in areas nominally under Palestinian control.
energy_note: Your bad signal is a planning decision.
notes: See TEC-001 for the spectrum side of the same problem.

aspect: The land is still yours on paper
description: Ownership is not extinguished; use is. A family can hold a deed to land it may not build on, plant on, fence, or reach without coordination.
energy_note: Owning a field you are not allowed to walk into.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the mast that cannot be built
description: Palestinian operators cannot readily erect telecom towers in Area C, which is over 60% of the West Bank and sits between every Palestinian population centre. The result is poor coverage inside Areas A and B, which are nominally under Palestinian control - a planning refusal in one area degrading a service in another.
energy_note: Bad signal in your own city, decided in a planning office.
